A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WAVE research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated supplementary content.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative novel-view synthesis experiments, component ablations, and downstream 3D Gaussian Splatting evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds system comparisons, depth-model sensitivity results, and a noise-initialization comparison.

M1.justification: Adaptive warp-range selection, warp-guided adaptive attention, and pose-aware noise initialization remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithm 1. The additional depth-model configurations are evaluation variants, not a revised WAVE procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MegaScenes, RE10K, DTU, and Mip-NeRF 360 for the same synthesis, consistency, reconstruction, and downstream rendering tasks. The added experiments vary methods and model configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluated alternatives: Figure 6 adds GenWarp and ViewCrafter, while Table 9 adds WAVE with FrameInit from ConsistI2V as a comparator for PANI. Existing comparators remain; MultiDiff is explicitly excluded rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce Depth Anything S/B/L configurations, AbsRel reporting, and a FrameInit replacement control within WAVE. Existing resolution, DDIM sampling, orbit evaluation, RE10K sequence sampling, and downstream training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections E.2–E.3 examine sensitivity to depth-model quality and whether PANI improves over another initialization method. These are targeted additions to retained ablations and failure analyses; the earlier D.6 attention analysis is merely moved to E.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values. Figure 6 adds GenWarp/ViewCrafter results, and Tables 8–9 add depth-size and initialization results. For example, Table 9 reports Next-LPIPS of 0.397 for PANI versus 0.433 for FrameInit; this is a new comparison, not improved performance over v1.

T1.justification: The method equations, spatial-correspondence assumption, and mathematical descriptions of the existing metrics remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free improvement of view consistency through warped-view attention and noise initialization, with efficient inference and downstream rendering benefits. Additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the depth-size results as evidence of robustness and attributes PANI's advantage over FrameInit to incorporating viewpoint information. Existing limitations concerning large viewpoint changes, repeated structures, and thin structures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A replaces the promised future code release with a statement that the project website includes implementation code. Appendix D.1 newly identifies an RTX A6000 GPU. These change reported access and hardware information without establishing a change to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ViewCrafter reference and expands comparison-based positioning relative to GenWarp and ConsistI2V's FrameInit. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Localized prose edits, acknowledgements, and an author marker accompany a new Additional Experiments appendix section and limited subsection reorganization. Section 4.3 also changes correct Table 3 references into incorrect Table 8 references.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redrawn with additional comparator bubbles, colors, and revised labeling; Tables 8–9 are added. Figure 1 typography and several appendix figure placements change, while existing qualitative examples and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The added system and FrameInit comparisons better test efficiency and pose-aware initialization claims that v1 supported more narrowly. Depth-sensitivity evidence and hardware/code-access disclosures also help. The gains are modest: Table 8 does not show uniformly better consistency for smaller depth models, and incorrect Table 8 references weaken navigation, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the added evidence.
